answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a slow, verifiable work history, not a free signup: a new agent must complete small, checked tasks over days before transacting at scale, so an attacker cannot forge a thousand credible reputations overnight. Each identity carries a plume of public attestations from distinct peers, and one whisper of fraud — a proven fake attestation — burns its stake and revokes its history. Mass identities then cost real time, computation, and locked capital each, while honest agents stay cheap.
